paper_title: Development and external validation of prediction algorithms to improve early diagnosis of cancer
prediction_task: Binary prediction of cancer diagnosis (any of multiple site-specific cancers) within 2 years of primary care presentation

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Time-horizon conflation: 2-year 'risk' of already-present cancer is a diagnostic probability, not a forward risk; imprecise use of 'risk' vs 'probability' obscures clinical purpose.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Revised terminology to 'probability' throughout; clarified outcome is diagnosis within 2 years used as proxy for as-yet-undiagnosed cancer.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Missing data in EHR shown to be MNAR; imputation method does not address this; missingness counts and potential bias not fully reported.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added Extended Table 1 with predictor completeness and Supplementary Table 13 comparing complete vs incomplete cases; noted demographic differences.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Model coefficients not published; code only available under academic license from Oxford University Innovations, hindering independent validation.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Software via academic license; authors declined to publish full coefficients table.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Calibration intercept/slope summary, key cancer-site-specific DCA, and cancer-site-specific sensitivity/specificity at 3% threshold should be in main text, not scattered across supplementary tables.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added calibration summary with intercept/slope values to main text; moved Supp Table 10 (site-specific sens/spec at 3% threshold) to Table 1; added DCA interpretation.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Variable selection based on P-value retention of predefined variables; automated selection with longer candidate variable list not considered.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Explained rationale: used P values with effect sizes (risk ratios) for parsimony; automated methods not well-extended to multinomial logistic models.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Model B (with blood tests) shows minimal improvement over Model A (clinical-only); added diagnostic value of blood tests unclear and clinical implications underdiscussed.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Clarified that Model B has higher sensitivity for 7 cancers (colorectal, blood, liver, lung, ovary, pancreas, prostate) but small overall discrimination gain and small net-benefit improvement.
